name: Stylometric Fingerprinting
description: Analyzes the multidimensional stylistic fingerprint of a text to determine authorship. Because Large Language Models are trained on vast, generalized datasets, their resulting textual output represents a statistical 'average' of human writing. They lack idiosyncratic quirks, producing prose that is highly structured, consistently formal, and stylistically sterile. Humans, on the other hand, leave distinct biometric-like traces in their writing—specific combinations of vocabulary richness, punctuation density, passive/active voice ratios, and favored transition phases that form a unique, lifelong stylistic signature.
mechanism: The algorithm computes a matrix of 50+ micro-stylometric markers, including hapax legomena (words used exactly once), comma frequency, syntactic branching depth, and function word distributions. It then maps these features into a high-dimensional vector space. If a text's stylometric vector lands squarely in the center of the 'universal average' distribution, it is overwhelmingly likely to be AI-generated. If the vector deviates significantly due to personal structural quirks, it strongly indicates a human author.
useCase: Highly effective for long-form analysis (essays, reports, literature) where there is enough raw data to reconstruct a stable, statistically significant profile of the author's voice.
strengths:
• Analyzes the fundamental architecture of the writer's thought process, making it highly resistant to simple paraphrasing or synonym-swapping tools.
• Capable of not just detecting AI, but differentiating between specific AI model families (e.g., GPT-4 vs. Claude 3) based on their distinct corporate alignment guidelines.
limitations:
• Requires a substantial amount of text (minimum 250-300 words) to build a stable stylometric profile; utterly useless on short social media posts.
• Multi-author collaborative documents or heavily edited texts can blur the stylistic fingerprint, causing false negatives.
parameters:
Analysis: 50+ Lexical, Syntactic, and Structural Markers
Metric: Multivariate Stylistic Derivation from Mean
Output: 0-100 Stylistic Homogeneity (Generic Authorship) Score
accuracy: High — 82-89% accuracy on longer documents. It is the gold standard for forensic document attribution and academic integrity auditing.

references.title: Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
Neal, T. et al. (2018). Surveying Stylometry Techniques and Applications. ACM Computing Surveys.
